part.name: Streamlined enclosure with central thumb wheel
part.description: A two-solid, mouse-like or handheld streamlined enclosure comprising a smooth asymmetric housing, an integrated rectangular wheel-support pedestal, and a separate rounded thumb wheel. The housing is formed from six large freeform surface patches, while the pedestal and wheel provide the principal mechanical interface.
part.symmetry_note: The part is approximately bilaterally symmetric about its longitudinal center plane, with paired left and right housing flanks and a centered wheel. It is not symmetric from end to end because one end is taller and more rounded while the opposite end is lower and more tapered.

Section.name: Main streamlined housing
features included: central opening or intersection region for the wheel-support pedestal
Section.function intent: Provide the primary enclosure, external gripping surface, protective shell, and load-bearing foundation for the central control interface.
Section.physical behavior: The broad freeform crown and base act as shell panels, while the side and end patches close the volume and distribute grip, impact, and wheel-actuation loads around the perimeter. Smooth curvature avoids local stress concentrations and provides an ergonomic external profile.
Section.geometry: A closed, elongated freeform body with two broad opposing B-spline surfaces, paired curved side flanks, a taller rounded end, and a lower tapered end. The upper broad surface contains an additional inner wire where the pedestal intersects or emerges from the housing.
Section.location: Forms the complete outer body and surrounds all other sections; elongated along the STEP z-axis, wide along x, and shallow along y.

major_faces.name: High-z rounded end cap
major_faces.description: Large four-sided B-spline patch closing the high-z end and blending into the crown and both side flanks.

major_faces.name: Left freeform flank
major_faces.description: Long convex B-spline sidewall forming the left perimeter of the enclosure.

major_faces.name: Lower base shell
major_faces.description: Broad, nearly planar but subtly shaped B-spline underside spanning most of the enclosure footprint.

major_faces.name: Low-z tapered end cap
major_faces.description: Curved B-spline patch closing the lower and more tapered end of the body.

major_faces.name: Right freeform flank
major_faces.description: Long convex B-spline sidewall opposing FACE 7 and forming the right perimeter.

major_faces.name: Upper crown shell
major_faces.description: Largest B-spline surface forming the ergonomic upper crown; its second wire corresponds to the central pedestal intersection region.

Section.name: Wheel-support pedestal
Section.function intent: Raise, locate, and laterally constrain the thumb wheel relative to the housing while transferring user input loads into the main shell.
Section.physical behavior: The paired thin side walls resist transverse wheel loads, the upper and lower walls maintain pedestal spacing, and the end wall closes and stiffens the rectangular support. Its embedded end blends or terminates in the housing, allowing wheel forces to enter the enclosure as bending and shear loads.
Section.geometry: A narrow, slightly inclined rectangular prismatic feature centered on the housing. Five planar faces are exposed; the remaining end is merged into or intersected by the main housing.
Section.location: Centered laterally on the upper region of the housing, extending approximately from y=10 to y=28 and between z=43.5 and z=59.3 in STEP coordinates.

major_faces.name: Pedestal upper longitudinal wall
major_faces.description: Narrow planar wall at the high-z edge of the rectangular pedestal.

major_faces.name: Pedestal left side wall
major_faces.description: Large planar side of the pedestal with a near-positive-x surface normal.

major_faces.name: Pedestal exposed end wall
major_faces.description: Rectangular planar closure at y=10 joining all four longitudinal pedestal walls.

major_faces.name: Pedestal right side wall
major_faces.description: Large planar side opposing FACE 0 and providing the other lateral locating wall.

major_faces.name: Pedestal lower longitudinal wall
major_faces.description: Narrow planar wall at the low-z edge of the rectangular pedestal.

Section.name: Thumb wheel
Section.function intent: Provide a compact finger-operated control surface, likely for rolling, scrolling, indexing, or pressing along the centerline of the enclosure.
Section.physical behavior: The toroidal outer bands present a smooth contact surface that accepts tangential or normal finger force. The planar side faces define the wheel thickness and can act as lateral locating surfaces. The wheel is a separate solid and is positioned to move or rotate relative to the support, although no explicit axle or bore is represented in the supplied B-rep.
Section.geometry: A thin rounded wheel or lenticular control body whose principal axis is approximately parallel to the STEP x-axis. Two toroidal patches form the convex perimeter and terminate at two opposing planar side faces.
Section.location: Centered above and partially within the pedestal near x=28, y=22, z=51 in STEP coordinates.

major_faces.name: Left wheel side face
major_faces.description: Planar rounded side of the wheel on the lower-x side, bounded by a single closed edge.

major_faces.name: Left toroidal contact band
major_faces.description: Toroidal freeform band blending outward from the left planar side and forming part of the finger-contact perimeter.

major_faces.name: Right toroidal contact band
major_faces.description: Opposing toroidal band completing the rounded contact perimeter and blending toward the right side.

major_faces.name: Right wheel side face
major_faces.description: Planar rounded side of the wheel on the higher-x side, opposing FACE 12.
